title: Format Specifiers and I/O
description: printf(), scanf(), getchar()/putchar(), format specifiers, and common scanf mistakes.
objectives: Use printf() with the correct format specifiers for each type
Use scanf() correctly, including the address-of operator

content.heading: printf() and Format Specifiers
content.body: printf(format, args...) writes formatted output. Common format specifiers: %d (int), %u (unsigned int), %f (float/double, defaulting to 6 decimal places — %.2f for two), %c (a single char), %s (a null-terminated string, char*), %ld/%lld (long/long long), %x (hexadecimal), and %p (a pointer address). Getting a specifier wrong for the argument's actual type is undefined behavior — printf trusts the format string completely and has no way to verify the argument's real type at runtime, so a mismatch typically produces garbage output rather than an error.

content.heading: scanf(), getchar(), and putchar()
content.body:
scanf(format, ...) reads formatted input, and crucially requires the address of each variable to write into, via the & operator: scanf("%d", &age); — forgetting & is one of the most common C mistakes, since scanf then receives whatever garbage value age currently holds interpreted as an address, and attempts to write through it (usually crashing). scanf() returns the number of items successfully read/assigned, which should be checked before trusting the resulting values — unchecked, malformed input silently leaves variables at whatever value (often uninitialized garbage) they had before the call.

getchar() reads a single character from standard input (returning it as an int, so EOF, a value outside the normal char range, can be represented); putchar(c) writes a single character to standard output — useful for simple, character-by-character processing without the overhead of scanf/printf's format parsing.

content.explanation: &age gives scanf the address it needs to write into. Checking scanf's return value against 1 (the expected number of successfully-read items) catches invalid input before age is used.

keyPoints: printf/scanf format specifiers must exactly match the argument's actual type
scanf() requires the address of each destination variable, via &
scanf()'s return value (items successfully read) should be checked, not assumed
getchar()/putchar() handle single-character I/O without format-string parsing overhead
commonMistakes: Forgetting & before a variable in a scanf() format argument
Using the wrong format specifier for a variable's actual type
Not checking scanf()'s return value and using a variable that was never actually assigned by malformed input
